first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, so simplifying onboarding addresses both current problems and has prior evidence of improving time-to-value and early adoption. Verify the onboarding and activation records before committing. Use a guarded test with downstream qualification and qualified-revenue metrics, since higher completion could otherwise reduce lead quality. Promotional pricing may counter competitor pressure, but it risks attracting lower-value accounts and does not directly address the onboarding decline.

final.rationale: Run a standard, guarded onboarding simplification experiment because completion is down 4% and the verified result shows a substantial completion lift, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and 3% higher 30-day retention. The verified activation-messaging result supports monitoring activation as a secondary outcome, but onboarding simplification is the single intervention most directly aligned with the current completion decline. Evaluate qualified pipeline, conversion quality, retention, and revenue—not just completion—to avoid trading downstream value for superficial funnel gains.
